Review
OSHI can\'t switch another app off. If you don\'t recognise one of these, turn it off in Android Settings › Accessibility, or uninstall it.
Apps can read or control this screen
%1$s. Strict security mode hides OSHI from them where Android allows it.
Dismiss
What it does
No copy, cut, forward, share or save of messages. Text can\'t be selected, and anything OSHI put on the clipboard is wiped.
Paste into OSHI is blocked when “Block paste too” is on, including the keyboard\'s paste command.
Screenshots, screen recording and screen sharing show a black screen. The recent-apps preview is hidden.
Apps that read the screen through Accessibility, including AI agents, see no OSHI content (Android 14 and later). Taps they inject are ignored.
Taps are ignored while another app draws over OSHI.
Notifications only say “New message”: no name, no photo, no text.
App lock every time you come back to OSHI (when your phone has a screen lock).
Incognito keyboard: the keyboard is asked not to learn what you type.
No link previews and no GIPHY search: nothing is fetched from third-party sites.
Read receipts and typing indicators off (if you chose to hide them).
Privacy relay turned on when one is available.
Your previous settings come back when you turn the mode off.
What it cannot do
No app can fully protect you from malware or from a compromised (rooted) phone.
Your keyboard still sees what you type. A clipboard suggestion it types for you can\'t be told apart from typing.
Screen readers for blind and low-vision people keep working, but other accessibility apps can\'t read OSHI while the mode is on.
On Android 13 and older, OSHI can\'t hide its content from accessibility apps. It can only warn you about them.
Someone can still photograph the screen with another device.
It protects this phone only, not the phones of the people you write to.
